title: Exact invertible twists and closure of eventual cohomology vanishing
statement:
Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], and let $\mathcal L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Tensor products and powers mean [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], with $\mathcal L^{\otimes0}=\mathcal O_X$; cohomology means the right derived functors of global sections [pqf-def-cohomology]. For a coherent module $\mathcal E$ [pqf-def-coherent] define
$$\mathcal P_{\mathcal L}(\mathcal E)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\exists n_0\in\mathbf N\;\forall n\ge n_0\;\forall p\ge1,\quad H^p(X,\mathcal E\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes n})=0.$$
Then:
(1) For every $n\ge0$, $\mathcal L^{\otimes n}$ is invertible, and $-\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes n}$ is an additive exact functor on $\mathcal O_X$-modules. Consequently the functors $\mathcal E\mapsto H^p(X,\mathcal E\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes n})$ are additive and take every short exact sequence [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] to its long exact cohomology sequence. In particular they preserve finite direct sums.
(2) The zero module has $\mathcal P_{\mathcal L}$. For a short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal E_1\to\mathcal E\to\mathcal E_2\to0$ of coherent modules, if the end terms have $\mathcal P_{\mathcal L}$, then the middle term does, with the maximum of any two witnessing bounds as a witnessing bound.
(3) Every finite direct sum of coherent modules is coherent, including the empty sum. If $\mathcal E$ is coherent and $r\ge1$, $\mathcal P_{\mathcal L}(\mathcal E^{\oplus r})$ implies $\mathcal P_{\mathcal L}(\mathcal E)$ with the same witnessing bound. Here $\mathcal E^{\oplus r}$ is the direct sum of $r$ copies of $\mathcal E$.

source.place: Tag 0B5V, lemma-surjective-finite-morphism-ample, verification of conditions (1) and (2) of Tag 01YM, lemma-property-higher-rank-cohomological; zero case explicit

proof.text: Induct on $n$. The power at $0$ is $\mathcal O_X$, locally free of rank one; the invertible tensor-product assertion of [lem-pc-tensor-dual-invertible] gives the successor. Each power is therefore finite locally free of rank one. Apply [lem-sc-ext-tensor-exact] to it and use the symmetry of [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed] to obtain exactness of $T_n=-\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes n}$ from exactness of left tensoring. The latter node also gives additivity of $T_n$.

The module category is abelian with enough injectives by [lem-sc-ringed-space-module-sheaves-enough-injectives], and $\Gamma(X,-)$ is additive and left exact by [lem-sc-global-sections-left-exact]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-universal-delta-functor] applies: every $H^p(X,-)=R^p\Gamma(X,-)$ is additive and the derived functors form a long exact sequence on every short exact sequence. Apply this to the short exact sequence obtained using $T_n$ in Step 1. Composition with the additive $T_n$ gives additivity of $A_{n,p}(\mathcal E)=H^p(X,T_n\mathcal E)$.

Write $A=A_{n,p}$. For a finite sum with inclusions $i_j$ and projections $q_j$, $q_ji_k=\delta_{jk}$ and $\sum_j i_jq_j=1$. Additivity and functoriality from Step 2 preserve both identities; the maps $(A(q_j))_j$ and $\sum_j A(i_j)$ are inverse. Hence $A$ preserves finite sums. For the zero module, $1_0=0$ implies $1_{A(0)}=A(1_0)=A(0)=0$, so $A(0)=0$. Thus every $n\ge0$ and $p\ge1$ vanishes for the zero module, and $n_0=0$ witnesses its property.

source.place: Tag 0B5V, lemma-surjective-finite-morphism-ample, additivity in condition (2); empty sum made explicit

proof.text: Let $b_1,b_2$ witness the property for the two end terms of the given short exact sequence. If $n\ge\max(b_1,b_2)$ and $p\ge1$, the long exact sequence of Step 2 contains $0=H^p(X,T_n\mathcal E_1)\to H^p(X,T_n\mathcal E)\to H^p(X,T_n\mathcal E_2)=0$. Exactness says that every element of the middle group is the image of zero, so the group is zero. The bound is independent of $p$ and is precisely $\max(b_1,b_2)$.

source.place: Tag 0B5V, lemma-surjective-finite-morphism-ample, verification of condition (1) of Tag 01YM

proof.text: Apply clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-modules-kernel-cokernel-sum] to the finite family of coherent modules. It gives coherence of their sum, including the zero module when the family is empty. In particular $\mathcal E^{\oplus r}$ is coherent, so the property used in the last assertion is defined.

source.place: Tag 01BY, lemma-coherent-abelian, coherent finite sums including zero

proof.text: For $r\ge1$ choose one summand inclusion $i:\mathcal E\to\mathcal E^{\oplus r}$ and its projection $q$, so $qi=1$. Functoriality gives $A_{n,p}(q)A_{n,p}(i)=1$. If $b$ witnesses vanishing for the sum, then for every $n\ge b$ and $p\ge1$ this composite factors through the zero group. Therefore the identity on $A_{n,p}(\mathcal E)$ is zero and that group is zero. The same $b$ works for $\mathcal E$.
